iconicAnchor.label: Charles Joseph Minard's flow maps
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Library of Congress shows how direction, width, geography, color, labels, and numerical units make magnitude and movement legible in a unified composition.

sources.title: 19th Century Colonization and Slavery in Charles Minard's Flow Maps
supports: Minard's proportional flow bands encode direction and amount between origins and destinations while labels and geography support rapid interpretation.

sources.title: The Minard System
supports: Minard's body of work represents a coherent historical system of statistical graphics for social, economic, geographic, and multivariate data.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/classic-infographic/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
